items.title: Don Menza and Sam Noto interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, January 28, 1997
items.q: I mean it’s nothing short of Gene Kelly and Fred Astaire.

ctx.x: He loved those upstate players because there was a certain energy coming from the upstate people you know, right from Buffalo all the way down to New York.

And you know of course the great line from Buddy Rich when he was getting ready to go in for brain surgery. The anesthesiologist asked him, they were getting ready to wheel him in and they said, “Mr. Rich, is there anything you know of that you’re allergic to?” “Yeah,” he says, “country music.” On his death bed, he still had that kind of wry sense of humor. I have a video somebody just sent me, of Buddy Rich singing and dancing and playing. I mean it’s an hour long video of him on “The Ed Sullivan Show,” on this…
I saw him in Batavia, New York, a long time ago.
